action: Place probe in the median of the body, specifically the right epigastrium. Instruct patient: 'Take a deep breath and hold it'.
interpretation: Prepare to scan the liver from the epigastric window.

action: Orient probe to obtain a cross-section (transverse view) of the left liver lobe.
interpretation: Visualize the transverse cross-section of the left liver lobe.

action: Instruct patient: 'Exhale, then inhale again and hold it'. Move probe to the right epigastrium.
interpretation: Reposition to the right epigastrium to transition views.

action: Maintain position in the right epigastrium.
interpretation: Evaluate the right liver lobe.

action: Assess image quality for obstructions.
interpretation: Note if visualization is difficult or if there are 'blank parts' in the right liver lobe due to air in the colon or post-prandial status (patient ate two hours ago).

action: Instruct patient: 'Put your right arm over your head'.
interpretation: Modify patient position to open intercostal spaces.

action: Instruct patient: 'Take a deep breath again'.
interpretation: Utilize inspiration to push the liver inferiorly.

action: Observe the monitor while maintaining probe position.
interpretation: Confirm that the picture quality is improving.

action: Assess the view.
interpretation: Determine that the view is still not optimal.

action: Instruct patient: 'Can you turn around to the left side a little bit?'. Confirm position: 'Yeah, that's good'.
interpretation: Reposition patient into Left Lateral Decubitus (LLD) to displace bowel gas.

action: Instruct patient: 'Take a deep breath again'.
interpretation: Re-establish inspiration in the new position.

action: Scan the right liver lobe.
interpretation: Visualize the right liver with improved clarity.

action: Move probe to obtain standard cross-sections of the center of the liver.
interpretation: Transition to standard central liver views.

action: Angle probe cranially to the most superior cross-section.
interpretation: Visualize the 'liver vein star' (hepatic veins) joining into the Inferior Vena Cava (IVC). Identify the IVC structure.

action: Instruct patient: 'Exhale again, take a deep breath, and hold it'.
interpretation: Refresh the breath-hold to maintain the window.

action: Slide probe inferiorly to the next standard cross-section.
interpretation: Identify the 'jumping stag sign'.

action: Hold probe steady on the stag sign.
interpretation: Visualize the components of the stag: horns, body, and legs. Identify this structure as the portal vein branching in the center of the liver.

action: Instruct patient: 'Exhale again'. Then: 'Take a deep breath again'.
interpretation: Prepare for the next anatomical landmark.

action: Scan to locate the boundary between lobes.
interpretation: Evaluate the echogenic line between the right and left liver lobes. Identify this as the interlobar ligament, ending in the teres hepatis ligament.

action: Instruct patient: 'Exhale again'. Then: 'Take a deep breath again'.
interpretation: Refresh the breath-hold.

action: Follow the anatomy corresponding to the 'tail' of the jumping stag sign. Instruct patient: 'Exhale again'.
interpretation: Locate the gallbladder at the end of the stag's tail.

action: Rotate probe to a long section (longitudinal) through the body.
interpretation: Prepare to evaluate the left liver lobe in a long section.

action: Instruct patient: 'Take a deep breath again and hold it'.
interpretation: Optimize the longitudinal window.

action: Scan the left side of the image.
interpretation: Visualize the filled stomach on the right side of the screen and identify the entrance into the stomach.

action: Focus on the boundary between thoracic and abdominal cavities. Instruct patient: 'Exhale again'.
interpretation: Identify the diaphragm as a small echogenic line between the heart and the liver.

action: Instruct patient: 'Take a deep breath again'.
interpretation: Re-inflate lungs to displace liver inferiorly.

action: Push the probe towards the patient's right side to reach the liver center.
interpretation: Visualize two distinct vascular structures.

action: Compare the walls of the visible vessels.
interpretation: Identify the echogenic circling (connective tissue) around the portal vein branch. Contrast this with the structure having NO echogenic structure around it.

action: Maintain view of the hepatic vasculature.
interpretation: Identify the vessel without connective tissue as a liver vein (hepatic vein). Confirm the difference: Portal veins have connective tissue (echogenic walls), liver veins do not.

action: Instruct patient: 'Exhale again'. Then: 'Take a deep breath again'.
interpretation: Prepare to move to the right lobe.

action: Move probe further to the patient's right.
interpretation: Visualize the right liver lobe, specifically the right portal vein and the gallbladder.

action: Move probe gradually down (inferiorly) towards the liver edge.
interpretation: Scan to the caudal end of the liver.

action: Hold position at the inferior liver edge.
interpretation: Visualize the right kidney appearing.

action: Instruct patient: 'Exhale again and lie back'.
interpretation: Relax the patient; scan complete for this position.

action: Move probe to a transcostal (intercostal) position.
interpretation: Adopt a transcostal view if anterior views are obscured by 'too much air in the colon'.

action: Find a sound window between ribs. Tilt the probe while maintaining position.
interpretation: Evaluate the right liver lobe and central structures (like the portal vein) through the costal window.
